component.name: Pulse-Vault
component.summary: Local encrypted file vault for Linux desktops

description.p: Pulse-Vault is a local-first encrypted file vault for Linux desktops. Keep sensitive files private in a single portable .pulsevault container with no cloud, no telemetry, and no accounts.

It uses authenticated encryption (ChaCha20-Poly1305 + AES-GCM cascade), memory-hard Scrypt key derivation (standard or hardened profiles), and LZMA compression. Large files are streamed so memory usage stays reasonable.

The app features a modern Yaru-aligned GUI for Ubuntu and other Linux desktops, plus a powerful guided CLI for headless, scripting, server, or packaging use (pip, apt, snap). Includes direct integration with GitHub Releases for downloads, clickable version info, and About dialog guidance.

ul.li: Strong offline password-based encryption with streaming for large files
Password rotation with full re-encryption of vault contents
Optional carrier file disguise (append vault to image or video)
Drag & drop import, Secure Open (temp extract + launch app), folder import
Native Linux desktop integration (desktop file, MIME type registration, AppStream metainfo)
Built-in links to GitHub Releases and official site from sidebar, version badge, and About

description.p: Perfect for journalists, developers, security researchers, privacy-conscious users, or anyone who wants strong local file privacy on Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 and other Linux desktops.
Pulse-Vault 0.0.21 brings a much more polished desktop experience and solid preparation for distribution.

The GUI now sports Ubuntu 26.04 Yaru-inspired theming with the signature orange accent color, refined dark/light palettes, consistent rounded corners, Ubuntu font preference, and better spacing and button styling so it feels right at home on modern Linux desktops.

We finally fixed the long-standing CLI vs GUI import coupling. The guided CLI (pulse-vault --cli and the dedicated pulse-vault-cli entry) no longer pulls in any tkinter or customtkinter code, making it genuinely suitable for headless, server, pip, apt, and Snap environments.

Documentation and packaging received major love: expanded AppStream metainfo with proper releases, keywords, screenshots placeholders, and store-ready details; updated INSTALL.md, README, and other docs with clear pip + App Store guidance; added desktop file validation and AppStream checks to CI.

Testing is in great shape — the full suite passes cleanly (92 tests), CLI/GUI isolation is enforced with fresh subprocess checks, and the Hypothesis-based security property tests are robust with better tamper coverage. We performed thorough internal reviews for security, UI, and packaging.
Changelog and release process got a refresh toward more human-readable notes while staying compatible with automation.
Improved packaging, CLI decoupling, Yaru-aligned UI polish for Ubuntu 26.04.
Added comprehensive CLI tests, advanced Hypothesis property/fuzz tests with security report artifact, GitHub release automation, and expanded CI.

GUI enhancements: always-visible GitHub Releases sidebar button, clickable version badge, dedicated GitHub Downloads & Releases dialog and About section, updated empty state messaging. All point users to packaged downloads.
Internal: larger I/O buffers, single-pass hashing+encrypt, header-only unlock probe, improved Scrypt threading and KDF persistence.
Fixed headless GUI construction in CI and minor UI typos.
Enhanced test coverage, CLI improvements, and packaging prep for future stores.
Core vault streaming, carrier file support, password policy, and early desktop files (MIME + .desktop).
Initial public development release with core encryption, GUI, and CLI.
